title: A Lantern for the Typewriter
premise: In the river town of Vellmarch, on the eve of revolution, Bram Winterbourne works her late father's type foundry disguised as his son, cutting letters by lamplight while the city's grievances pile up in print. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the master ledger containing every name of the resistance's dead and disappeared, Bram discovers the ledger was hidden inside a hollowed typewriter case in her own cellar — evidence that could condemn or save hundreds. She must carry it past three checkpoints to the foreign press office across the border, guided by a disgraced army clerk who once signed the requisition orders. At the final checkpoint she is recognized, and she chooses to burn her own forged identity papers rather than the ledger, testifying openly under her true name; the ledger reaches the presses, the town's names are printed and scattered like lanterns, and Bram survives not by staying invisible but by being seen.
about_author: Elodie Nystrom is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in Baltic port towns before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about people whose work leaves marks on the world they cannot sign.

chapters.title: The Weight of Letters
chapters.summary: Bram, working as 'Bram' the son of the dead type cutter Aldous Winterbourne, finishes a run of pamphlets at night while soldiers drill in the square below. POV: Bram. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine — the reader learns what it costs to be invisible.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: The resistance printer Oskar reveals that the master ledger of the disappeared has been moved again, and that its hiding place is known only to a dead man. POV: Bram. Beat: unease; Bram realizes her father kept secrets she never asked about.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: At dawn, Colonel Hessler's men seal the town and post requisition orders on every door: all presses, paper, and records are property of the army. POV: Bram. Beat: shock hardening into resolve as she watches her livelihood become contraband.

chapters.title: The Hollow Case
chapters.summary: Searching her father's cellar, Bram finds the ledger sewn into the lining of a battered typewriter case he left behind. POV: Bram. Beat: grief and awe — her father trusted her with this without ever telling her.

chapters.title: A Clerk's Signature
chapters.summary: Army clerk Elias Rehn, who processed the requisition, recognizes the foundry stamp on seized type and begins quietly pulling files. POV: Elias. Beat: guilt surfacing; he knows exactly what the ledger means and who will die if it burns.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Oskar maps the route to the border press office: the grain gate, the river ferry, the mountain pass. Each has a different master. POV: Bram. Beat: cold clarity — the plan is simple and almost certainly fatal.

chapters.title: Learning to Be No One
chapters.summary: Bram rehearses a new identity: a widow hauling her husband's useless typewriter to relatives. She practices walking, weeping on command, forgetting her own hands. POV: Bram. Beat: eerie self-erasure; invisibility as craft.

chapters.title: The First Crack
chapters.summary: Soldiers search the foundry and find fresh ink where no work should be done. Sergeant Duvall suspects the 'son' who never appears in daylight. POV: Bram. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Elias Asks a Question
chapters.summary: Elias interviews townsfolk about missing records and meets Bram, asking one question too precisely. Neither lies well enough. POV: Elias. Beat: mutual recognition between two people pretending.

chapters.title: Oskar's Price
chapters.summary: Oskar admits he traded names to survive an earlier purge; the ledger contains his confession too. He wants it destroyed, not delivered. POV: Oskar. Beat: betrayal reframed — even allies have reasons to want silence.

chapters.title: The Grain Gate
chapters.summary: First checkpoint: Bram passes through amid carts of confiscated wheat, the typewriter case under burlap, while a soldier jokes about widows and their junk. POV: Bram. Beat: vertiginous relief that curdles when she sees a neighbor arrested behind her.

chapters.title: Duvall Closes In
chapters.summary: Sergeant Duvall matches ink samples to the foundry and requests authority to detain the Winterbourne heir. POV: Duvall. Beat: rising menace; the hunt acquires a face.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: At the river, the old ferryman Marta owes Bram's father a debt measured in printed obituaries; she agrees to hide Bram below deck. POV: Marta. Beat: warmth in a cold chapter — memory as currency.

chapters.title: What Elias Signed
chapters.summary: Elias rereads his own requisition orders and realizes he condemned the foundry personally. He requests transfer to the river checkpoint. POV: Elias. Beat: shame becoming motion toward redemption.

chapters.title: Storm on the Water
chapters.summary: The ferry is boarded mid-river during a storm; Bram hides in the bilge while soldiers confiscate passengers' papers above. POV: Bram. Beat: terror and claustrophobia; the ledger nearly slips into floodwater.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint
chapters.summary: River checkpoint: Elias himself processes the manifests and, recognizing the typewriter case, stamps Bram through without searching — then follows her off the dock. POV: Bram/Elias alternating. Beat: uneasy alliance born at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Elias confronts Bram on the road: he wants the ledger delivered as much as she does, because his name is in it as an instrument, not a victim. They bargain. POV: Elias. Beat: prickly trust; two liars agreeing to tell one truth together.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot
chapters.summary: They shelter in a village where the requisition already succeeded: no names on doors, no graves marked, a church registry burned. POV: Bram. Beat: horror as prophecy — this is Vellmarch's future without the ledger.

chapters.title: Duvall's Warrant
chapters.summary: Duvall obtains authorization to shoot fugitives on sight and posts Bram's description — including the detail that 'he' is a woman. POV: Duvall. Beat: the disguise collapses as protection; exposure looms.

chapters.title: Marta's Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Marta is arrested for aiding the ferry stowaway and refuses to speak, buying Bram three days. POV: Marta. Beat: grief and gratitude; the price of survival paid by someone else.

chapters.title: The Mountain Road
chapters.summary: Bram and Elias climb toward the pass, trading histories: her father's forge, his conscription, the first order he ever signed. POV: both. Beat: intimacy forged in exhaustion; the middle-book stillness before the fall.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Chapel
chapters.summary: Deserters rob them and discover the ledger, reading their own brothers' names aloud before letting them go — one deserter joins them. POV: Bram. Beat: unexpected mercy from the lawless; justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: Hessler's Summons
chapters.summary: Colonel Hessler, needing a traitor to pacify the town, accepts Duvall's theory and orders the foundry demolished with the family 'accounted for.' POV: Hessler. Beat: bureaucratic evil; the noose tightens without malice.

chapters.title: The Pass Closed
chapters.summary: Snow seals the mountain pass; the third checkpoint is the only way through, and word of a woman fugitive has reached its commander. POV: Bram. Beat: despair — every road now leads through recognition.

chapters.title: A Second Forgery
chapters.summary: Using her father's skills, Bram cuts a new identity overnight — type, seal, and all — knowing forgery at the checkpoint means hanging. POV: Bram. Beat: fierce competence; artistry as weapon.

chapters.title: Oskar's Letter
chapters.summary: A intercepted letter reveals Oskar sold the route to save himself; Duvall now waits at the pass. POV: Elias. Beat: betrayal landing like a blow; the plan was always a trap.

chapters.title: The Choice of Names
chapters.summary: Bram tells Elias the truth she buried: her real name, her father's design, why she became 'Bram.' For the first time she chooses which self survives. POV: Bram. Beat: catharsis; invisibility voluntarily set down.

chapters.title: Night Before the Pass
chapters.summary: The small company — Bram, Elias, the deserter — keeps watch, burning letters, sharpening resolve. The deserter volunteers to draw the sentries. POV: rotating. Beat: elegiac calm; the last night of the old life.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Lie
chapters.summary: Bram presents the forged papers; the commander hesitates over the seal while Duvall walks the line. The deserter's diversion erupts. POV: Bram. Beat: white-knuckle suspense.

chapters.title: Recognized
chapters.summary: Duvall looks directly at Bram and knows her — but hesitates, remembering the village with no names. His delay costs him; shots are fired. POV: Duvall. Beat: the hunter's crisis of conscience.

chapters.title: Flight Through Fire
chapters.summary: Chased into the treeline, Bram and Elias run with the case as the checkpoint burns behind them; the deserter falls covering their escape. POV: Bram. Beat: grief at full speed; survival feels like theft.

chapters.title: The Border Stone
chapters.summary: Within sight of the border press office, Elias is shot by a pursuing patrol. Dying, he makes Bram promise to print his signature beside the names. POV: Elias. Beat: devastating sacrifice; complicity redeemed in ink.

chapters.title: Alone With the Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram hides in a border barn, wounded, reading the ledger cover to cover — her neighbors, her father's notes, Elias's name added in her hand. POV: Bram. Beat: mourning transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Press Office Refuses
chapters.summary: The foreign editor fears war and refuses unverified documents. Bram, cornered, offers the one verification no one can fake: testimony under her true name. POV: Bram. Beat: the theme crystallizes — visibility as the only honest proof.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Bram gives sworn statement, cuts her name in type herself, and watches the first sheets come off the press bearing the ledger's contents. POV: Bram. Beat: triumph inseparable from cost.

chapters.title: The Lanterns
chapters.summary: Printed broadsheets flood back across the border by night, carried by ferrymen, deserters, farmers — each page a lantern lit for a name. POV: ensemble. Beat: the evidence escapes beyond anyone's power to recall.

chapters.title: Duvall's Report
chapters.summary: Ordered to declare the ledger destroyed, Duvall instead files the truth and resigns his commission, walking out of the army through the same grain gate. POV: Duvall. Beat: quiet justice outside the law's machinery.

chapters.title: Return to Vellmarch
chapters.summary: With the regime tottering, Bram returns to a half-ruined foundry and rehangs the sign with her father's name and, beneath it, her own. POV: Bram. Beat: homecoming without illusion.

chapters.title: The Trial of the Ledger
chapters.summary: A provisional court uses the ledger to try Hessler's officers; Bram testifies again, and Oskar, surrendering himself, reads his own confession aloud. POV: Bram/Oskar. Beat: accountability achieved through memory, not vengeance.

chapters.title: A Lantern for the Typewriter
chapters.summary: Years later, Bram sets type for the ledger's published edition, hangs a lantern over the restored typewriter case, and teaches apprentices that every letter cut is a name refused to oblivion. POV: Bram. Beat: resolution — survival justified by what it preserved.
